title: Operant Conditioning
subtitle: Consequences change the future probability of brain-state behaviours
altText: Chalkboard-style clinical diagram illustrating operant conditioning within a neurofeedback closed loop.
learningObjectives: Explain operant conditioning without diagnostic overreach.
Distinguish measurement, mechanism and clinical outcome in operant conditioning.
Identify one safety or validity limitation relevant to operant conditioning.

sections.explainSimply: When a measured brain pattern meets a target, the system delivers a reward such as clearer video or points.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: The reinforcement is contingent on a physiological feature rather than an overt action, although posture, gaze and muscle activity can accidentally control the reward if artifacts are not managed.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Effective shaping requires a genuine contingency, an achievable criterion and feedback close enough in time to the event being reinforced. Sham and yoked-feedback controls test whether specific contingency matters.
sections.thinkOfItLike: A driving instructor who gives immediate dashboard feedback while the learner practises a controllable skill.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Psychologists need to understand operant conditioning to evaluate mechanism claims, informed consent, treatment fit and whether change transfers to real-world function.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Rewarding artifact can produce impressive scores without meaningful neural learning.
sections.clinicalPearl: The trained metric is an intermediate target; the clinical endpoint is meaningful function.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician using operant conditioning predefines the target, checks raw signal and artifacts, monitors symptoms and function, and reviews whether change generalises beyond the feedback display.
sections.limitationsCautions: Rewarding artifact can produce impressive scores without meaningful neural learning. Evidence classification: established behavioural principle.

options: When a measured brain pattern meets a target, the system delivers a reward such as clearer video or points.
Protocol choice requires no outcome measurement
Artifact is irrelevant once feedback begins
quizBank.explanation: When a measured brain pattern meets a target, the system delivers a reward such as clearer video or points.

quizBank.question: Which limitation matters most when interpreting Operant Conditioning?
options: Rewarding artifact can produce impressive scores without meaningful neural learning.

quizBank.question: How should the evidence for Operant Conditioning be communicated?
options: As established behavioural principle, with methods and outcomes specified
As conclusively effective for all clients
By promising normalisation of the brain
quizBank.explanation: The appropriate evidence label is: established behavioural principle.
